name: Holstein dairy cow
prompt: Create a naturalistic adult female polled Holstein dairy cow in moderate body condition, with black-and-white markings. Show a grounded walk, subtle breathing, ear and tail motion, and a small jaw movement. Provide clay views for anatomical review.

sources.title: Purdue Extension: Hoof Anatomy, Care and Management in Livestock
sources.note: External reference only; no illustration is redistributed. Cattle have paired principal hoof digits; horses have one continuous hoof.

sources.title: University of Minnesota: Gait glossary
sources.note: Walk timing and contact terminology. Procedural motion is a simplified interpretation, not motion capture.

sources.title: Holstein Association USA: Holstein 101
sources.note: Breed appearance, mature size, and polled trait. Reference target only; the specimen is original and does not reproduce a named animal.

sources.title: Purebred Dairy Cattle Association unified scorecard
sources.note: Head, dairy frame, udder and breed identification review; judging guidance is not a measured population envelope.

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Learn To Score Body Condition
sources.note: Dairy 1-to-5 scale and visible pelvis/loin landmarks; target score requires visual review, not a software-certified assessment.

sources.title: Tijssen et al. (2021): Kinematic gait characteristics of straight line walk in clinically sound dairy cows
sources.note: Seventeen Swedish Red/Holstein cows walking at their selected pace on concrete; front/hind stance-fraction evidence informs gait interpretation. Study results do not define breed ranges or validate this procedural animation. Reference only; no figures, video or data files are bundled.

sources.title: Nuss et al. (2015): Kinetics of heifers and cows walking on an instrumented treadmill
sources.note: Primary-study abstract: ten cows and nine heifers, reported separately. Cow-subgroup means provide stride/speed/cadence context, not prescribed settings or Holstein limits. Reference only; no article assets are bundled.

evidence.notes: Adult female dairy animal is the selected reference profile; the generated specimen is not a measured individual.
Broad muzzle, angular dairy frame, four limbs and an udder are modeled from breed and anatomical guidance. Original control surface requires review.
Baseline size and body relationships use breed references. All multipliers are engineering controls; their accepted interval is not a scientifically established range.
Two principal weight-bearing claws per foot, separated by an interdigital cleft. Verify both digits in geometry.
Black-and-white piebald coat is supported. Exact patch placement is seeded and invented, not copied from reference photographs.

Four-beat walking is interpreted from the glossary and cow-study context. The .68/.64 front/hind stance fractions are informed by study results; the 1.4 m baseline full stride, 1.0 m/s speed, approximately 6.7-degree peak absolute swing hoof pitch, and joint/body trajectories are authored animation settings. These are not motion capture or validated Holstein limits; review the complete cycle and actual hoof-shell contact.
Polled is a documented Holstein trait. This selected individual is naturally hornless; that is not a claim all Holsteins are polled.
Target 3/5, moderate dairy condition. Pelvis and loin landmarks must be checked in clay renders.
Deterministic original patch arrangement; no external image texture.

notes: Original procedural anatomy study; anatomical and visual approval pending.
Selected as an adult cow in mid-lactation. The udder is an external simplified representation, not internal anatomy.
Jaw movement is a limited illustrative motion and does not simulate chewing or rumination.
Breathing, blinking, ears and tail are interpreted motion. No live animal measurements or motion capture are claimed.
Reference images are linked, not bundled. Original geometry/material generation is covered by the repository license.
Gait distances, stance fractions and hoof flexion are original authored animation controls informed by linked study context. Numeric contact checks do not establish anatomical or visual approval.
